transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
Seven U.S. senators are calling on President Trump to reverse course on his diesel deal
with Russia.
NPR's Luke Garrett reports the bipartisan group of senators say the agreement is illegal.
On Friday, Trump shocked lawmakers when he announced the deal with Russian President
Vladimir Putin.
Trump said the agreement would immediately supply U.S. and international markets with
hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel.
On Sunday, three Democrats and four Republicans said Trump's deal is illegal because Congress
"explicitly banned Russian energy imports" in 2022.
Here's GOP Senator Tom Tillis on NBC News.
I do believe there's a legitimate case for saying the president's not following the law.
We were very clear that Russia is the aggressor, Russia is the one who can end this war by backing
out of territory that they occupied.
The seven senators called on Trump to "immediately reverse course" on his oil deal with Russia.
Following the war with Iran, the high cost of gas has hurt Trump politically.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
The Justice Department is investigating five American television networks under antitrust
laws amid a related court battle between the White House and press access.
As NPR's David Falkenflick reports, the move represents an escalation of tensions between
the president and the media.
CNN, Politico, and MS now sued after President Trump banned their journalists from the White
House over coverage that angered him.
A federal judge temporarily required the administration to restore their passes.
He says he'll decide by Tuesday evening.
In the meantime, the White House blocked CNN from taking part in the TV pool, in which ABC,
CBS, CNN, Fox News, and NBC shared logistical planning and costs to cover the president in
his public appearances in smaller spaces.
The other networks refused to fill the pool when CNN had been blocked.
The Justice Department now says it's investigating that consultation, claiming it may constitute
illegal antitrust behavior.
Media advocates say it's another attempt to intimidate the press.
David Falkenflick, NPR News.
On both coasts, they are dealing with flooding and high winds in the aftermath of two hurricanes.
NPR's Shonda Lee Stuster has the story.
The remnants of East Ayes and Rachel, now post-tropical cyclones, have caused flooding
across the South and West.
In North Carolina, there were tornado warnings on Sunday, as well as a high risk of flooding
from heavy rains.
Rapid river rising is also possible as the system moves out.
A tornado watch is also in effect for parts of Southern Virginia through Sunday night.
The National Weather Service says parts of the Southwest, including Southern California,
could receive up to three inches of rain on Sunday.
Forecasters also warned of damaging winds and life-threatening surf, as well as rip currents.
Rain is expected to continue from both East Ayes and Rachel through Monday.
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Pope Leo announced today he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a nodule that
was discovered in one of his lungs.
The Vatican says the recovery time for the Chicago-born 71-year-old pontiff should take
about a week.
Speaking to a crowd at St. Peter's Square, the pope told worshippers today the nodule
he said was found at a very early stage, and his doctors have recommended surgery.
The surgery is due to occur at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, which is the primary location for
popes to receive medical attention.
Pope Leo has no previous known health problems.
It's pumpkin spice season, and some shoppers are paying a lot more for their fall-themed
products.
NPR's Stephen Bassaha reports prices for the pumpkin flavors cost more than last year.
There's an almost 9 percent pumpkin spice premium, up a bit from last year.
Matt Schultz is chief consumer finance analyst at Lending Tree, which did the research.
He says some of the spooky season bump could be because pumpkins are slightly more expensive
this year.
But also, retailers understand how much people love pumpkin spice and how they might be willing
to pay a little bit extra for it.
Now, this does vary by store.
If you take the time to look around at different places, you might be able to save yourself
a little money.
Out of the six retailers it looked at, Lending Tree says Starbucks and Trader Joe's had the
biggest fall flavor hikes.
Stephen Bassaha, NPR News.
Key reports about the shape of the U.S. economy will be released this week Wednesday.
The September report on consumer inflation is expected.
Dan Ronan, NPR News, Washington.
Support for NPR.

Justice Department investigates five TV networks under antitrust laws amid CNN, Politico press access suit
Remnants of hurricanes East Ayes and Rachel bring flooding and tornado warnings to South and West
Pope Leo to undergo surgery in Rome to remove a lung nodule, recovery about a week
